topic.title: Active Learning and Selective Data Acquisition
topic.overview: Active learning chooses which observations should receive expensive labels or measurements. This topic studies uncertainty, diversity, coverage, and statistical inference when the learner controls data acquisition. Batch selection introduces an additional challenge: individually informative examples may be redundant when requested together, especially at large batch sizes.
topic.whyItMatters: The value of a query depends on the eventual goal, whether improving a classifier or estimating a statistical quantity. Selection can also amplify existing model biases, so class imbalance, annotation noise, and prior information need explicit treatment. Annotation savings must be measured at comparable predictive or inferential quality.
topic.evolution: A 1994 ensemble method uses disagreement to select new labels. Later representatives develop pool-based guarantees and information-based selection. Work in 2021 combines uncertainty and diversity for very large batches; a 2026 approach uses foundation-model priors with smaller models to guide acquisition under both class imbalance and noisy annotations.
openQuestions: How can query strategies discover examples that the current model confidently misunderstands?
When should acquisition prioritize minority coverage rather than maximal immediate uncertainty reduction?
